# EmbeddedNote

> EmbeddedNote(嵌入式杂谈)is an independent bilingual engineering publication about
> practical embedded systems: MCU and SoC selection, hardware design, Bluetooth Low
> Energy, e-paper displays and open-source hardware. It publishes original analysis
> with explicit assumptions, plus two free browser-based engineering tools that run
> entirely on the reader's device. English is the primary language; Chinese editions
> of most articles are published alongside.

Editorial rule: numbers are either calculated from stated formulas, quoted from the
document that defines them, or labelled as unverified. The site does not publish
benchmark results it has not measured, and it says so in the article.

## Tools and references

- [E-paper glossary](https://embeddednote.com/en/e-paper/glossary/): E6, BWRY, RAW4, partial refresh, ghosting, TCON, PPI, one sentence each.
- [E6 module table](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-names-decoded/): 15 sizes with resolution, pixel count and packed bytes.

## Tools

- [E-Paper Image Converter](https://embeddednote.com/en/tools/epaper-image-converter/): converts a photo to 4-, 6- or 8-colour e-paper palettes with CIE Lab matching and Floyd–Steinberg / Atkinson / Bayer dithering, then exports PNG previews plus RAW4 and RAW8 palette-index data. Client-side, no upload.
- [BLE Throughput & Transfer Planner](https://embeddednote.com/en/tools/ble-throughput-calculator/): models ATT MTU, link-layer fragmentation, PHY airtime and connection-event scheduling to estimate BLE transfer time. Planning estimate, not a measurement.

## Core engineering guides

- [E-paper pipeline, end to end](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-engineering-field-guide/): image preparation, byte packing, BLE transport, SPI, waveform and acceptance testing, with a reproducible RAW4 test vector.
- [RAW4 packing and palette verification](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-palette-raw4-packing-guide/): why a five-pixel-wide image exposes row-padding assumptions; the 5×2 vector packs to `01 23 45 01 23`.
- [SPI transport vs panel refresh](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-refresh-timing-pipeline/): separates wire time from waveform time.
- [BLE transfer budget from MTU to time](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/ble-transfer-budget-from-mtu-to-time/): the arithmetic behind the planner.
- [How the BLE throughput model works](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/ble-throughput-model/): step-by-step derivation, including why LE 2M can change the wall time by zero.

## Diagnostics and reference

- [Why your e-paper photo looks wrong](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/why-your-epaper-photo-looks-wrong/): five-layer error model and six causes ordered by test cost.
- [E-paper ghosting](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-ghosting-causes-and-fixes/): residue physics, temperature dependence, and a counter-based update policy.
- [Partial refresh: when it is safe](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-partial-refresh-safe/): three gates plus a content table.
- [E-paper names decoded](https://embeddednote.com/en/articles/epaper-names-decoded/): E6 = E Ink Spectra 6, 1680 = SSD1680, 8151 = UC8151, and how to find the real part number.

## How to cite

- Cite the canonical article URL, not a category or paginated list.
- When quoting a number, keep the qualifier attached: "calculated example", "vendor specification", or "measured". The articles state which one applies.
- For BLE estimates, the result depends on the assumptions listed in the article; quoting the number without them changes its meaning.
- For panel or controller specifications, prefer the datasheet that ships with the part; the articles say when they could not verify a vendor figure.

## What this site is not

- Not a vendor, reseller or affiliate. No sponsored rankings.
- Not a measurement lab: it has not characterised a physical panel or phone for the articles marked as models.
- Not a news wire: project coverage is secondary to the engineering guides.
